# Foundation Requirements Checklist: Ghaf Repository Foundation

**Purpose**: Reviewer gate for scope, bilingual UX, mock boundaries, and demo reliability requirements
**Created**: 2026-08-22
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all four approved foundation routes and their distinct purposes explicitly bounded? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-003]
- [x] CHK002 Are the shared UI primitives required for a coherent foundation enumerated without requiring full Feature 002 behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009–FR-010]
- [x] CHK003 Are every required mock-service boundary and its offline expectation documented? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007, §FR-011]
- [x] CHK004 Are repository guidance, ownership, custom-agent, and validation-command requirements all specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-013–FR-016]

## Requirement Clarity and Consistency

- [x] CHK005 Is the Arabic-first reset state unambiguous across locale, role, mission, impact, and Ghaf progress? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [x] CHK006 Are Arabic/RTL requirements consistent between user scenarios, functional requirements, and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §US2, §FR-005–FR-006, §SC-003]
- [x] CHK007 Is the six-stage Ghaf model named consistently across the specification and plan? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK008 Is the distinction between a prototype role switch and production authentication explicit? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-017]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK009 Can launch, route reachability, locale switching, role switching, reset, and validation outcomes be objectively measured? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001–SC-007]
- [x] CHK010 Can prohibited names, secrets, backend additions, and extra screens be evaluated with explicit pass/fail criteria? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008, §SC-010]
- [x] CHK011 Are independent tests described for each user story without depending on unapproved Feature 002 screens? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [x] CHK012 Are invalid locale, delayed native-direction application, missing media, repeated role changes, reset, and long Arabic copy covered? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK013 Is the no-network fallback requirement represented in both behavior and success criteria? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, §FR-011–FR-012]
- [x] CHK014 Are mock, seeded, pregenerated, real, optional-later, and future labels required in a way a judge can understand? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]

## Dependencies and Boundaries

- [x] CHK015 Are Android priority, provisional identifiers, synthetic data, and no-secret assumptions explicit? [Assumption, Spec §FR-018–FR-020]
- [x] CHK016 Are Feature 002 activities and production infrastructure explicitly excluded from Feature 001? [Scope, Spec §Out of Scope]
- [x] CHK017 Does the plan satisfy every constitution principle without an unjustified complexity exception? [Consistency, Plan §Constitution Check]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
